Thanks Vanessa — answered inline and added roster info below. TTL notes and assumptions included.

Quick answers for SIG cells (concise):
- Detection & internal triage: Redwood initiates incident triage within 1 hour of a confirmed detection (or credible report).
- Customer notification SLA: For incidents that materially affect a customer's data confidentiality or integrity (confirmed exfiltration or unauthorized access), Redwood commits to notify the affected customer(s) within 24 hours of confirmation. Notification includes summary of impact, immediate mitigations, and next steps.
- Regulator notification: Redwood's obligation to notify regulators depends on jurisdiction and breach criteria. We do not commit to regulator filing timelines in the SIG by default; we will work with customers on regulatory notifications and can coordinate disclosures per contract/legal guidance. If GreenFintech requires explicit regulator-window commitments, need legal sign-off.
- Follow-up cadence: initial notification within 24h, followed by a technical update within 72h, and periodic status updates every 72h until remediation or closure.

Escalation / roster (for SIG roster CSV):
- Rafael Mendes — Security Lead — rafael.mendes@redwood.com (primary security contact)
- Laura Bennett — Legal Counsel — laura.bennett@redwood.com (privacy & regulator questions)
- Marissa Cole — Customer Success Manager — marissa.cole@redwood.com (customer comms & remediation coordination)

Assumptions / caveats:
- "24 hours" refers to notification after internal confirmation of impact; detection-to-confirmation time varies by incident complexity.
- For incidents affecting multiple customers or industry-wide alerts, we may coordinate a single joint notification cadence.
- For regulated data subjects, Laura to advise on any mandatory filing windows.

I'll attach a CSV roster (IR-Roster-v1.csv) with the above lines. If Laura or Marissa want to tweak titles/emails for external-facing docs, flag edits.

-Rafael
